turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning doctor, just done Mr Jacobs. Creatinine is 168, eGFR 38, blood pressure 152 over 88, pulse 74. Chart has ramipril 5 milligrams daily.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ag shame. Last time they told us 150 for the creatinine. The ramipril though, no, the box at home is 10 milligrams, not 5.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks, sister. Mr Jacobs, howzit, come sit. What's today about then?
[SEG0004] person_4 (PATIENT): Sugar. Kidneys.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ja, diabetes and the kidneys. Wife's with you, that's fine by me. Any fever lately?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): On the chest side, any cough, wheeze, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the weight, up or down since last time?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): Umm. Sort of. Don't know.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hmm, not much to go on, we'll park the weight. Creatinine 168 with an eGFR of 38, that's stage 3b, err, on the background of the sugar. You still on the metforman?
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Metformin 500, morning and night. He skips the night one sometimes. I don't always see.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so 500 milligrams twice a day on paper, evenings hit and miss. Ramipril, chart says 5, you're saying the box is 10 in the morning?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ten. Every morning. I put it out.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): I won't guess between 5 and 10 till I see the box. We carry on with the ramipril either way, it protects the kidney even if the creatinine ticks up a little.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): eGFR is 38 so the metformin can stay, we'd only stop that under 30. You've been getting ibuprofin from the shop, haven't you?
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dis-Chem. Ibuprofen, the 200 milligram ones. Two when the knee is sore, so 400, not every day. You told him no.
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Knee.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): The right one?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Months now, that right knee.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok. Shop ibuprofen with ramipril and diabetic kidneys, I'm not happy. I'm thinking the creatinine of 168 is the ibuprofen sitting on the diabetic kidney disease.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Could also just be the kidney disease moving on by itself. I can't separate those two today.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): So ibuprofen stops. Paracetamol instead, one gram, two 500 milligram tablets, by mouth, up to three times a day for the knee, not more.
[SEG0026] person_4 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His sister Joyce takes biotin, the hair gummies. Hers, not his. I've got my own pressure tablets too, don't put those on him.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not his. Family, Mr Jacobs, any sugar or pressure in the relatives?
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties. Mother did not. My brother had a stroke at sixty. Another sister has pressure but no sugar.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): And an ordinary day, the job, hours, food, exercise, a drink?
[SEG0031] person_4 (PATIENT): I drive a bakkie for the municipality, six till three. Pap and meat most nights. I walk the dogs round the block. A beer on a Friday, that's it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep it to the Friday beer, hey. Looking now, no swelling at the ankles. Right knee's a bit bony, no heat. Chest is clear.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): So. Repeat creatinine and eGFR in two weeks, sister books that. Back here in six weeks with the ramipril box, then we settle 5 or 10. Paracetamol from today, and the ibuprofen stays in the cupboard.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book the bloods for two weeks, and the six week review at the desk.
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): Sharp.

spec.situation: Older diabetic with kidney disease on review; creatinine and eGFR read aloud; takes ibuprofen from a shop against advice; ramipril continued, painkiller advice changed.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Right knee pain and months duration supported; duration reported by family member, not patient.
bad.text: Right knee pain (category=musculoskeletal, status=present, duration=several months, temporality=current, body_site=right knee, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Ramipril charted dose is 5 mg daily, but the home box is reportedly 10 mg every morning; doctor explicitly said not to guess between 5 and 10 until the box is seen and to continue ramipril either way meanwhile.
Metformin should be continued because eGFR is 38, with the doctor's threshold to stop being eGFR under 30.
Metformin evening dose adherence issue: evenings are 'hit and miss' and the patient sometimes skips the night dose.
Ibuprofen source and tablet strength were specified: bought from Dis-Chem, 200 mg tablets, taken as two tablets (400 mg) when the knee is sore, not every day.
Doctor stated the creatinine had previously been about 150 according to family, implying a rise to 168.
Weight change was asked about but the patient was unsure, so weight history could not be established.
Negative family history details: mother did not have diabetes, and sister has hypertension but no diabetes.
Nurse-reported creatinine and eGFR results were available at the start of the visit along with vitals.
Follow-up logistics: nurse will book the repeat blood tests for two weeks and the six-week review at the desk.
